pr.title: gh-111178: fix UBSan failures in `Objects/typeobject.c`
pr.body:
This PR fixes the UBSan failures and addresses some minor cosmetic changes. PEP-7 changes were not applied since they could scramble the diff but other semantic changes affecting the signature of touched functions may have been done.

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-111178 -->
* Issue: gh-111178
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

auto_merge.commit_message:
Fix UBSan failures for `PyTypeObject`.
Introduce a macro cast for `superobject` and remove redundant casts.
Rename the unused parameter in getter/setter methods  to `closure`
for semantic purposes.

review_comments.body:
I don't think that inline is correct since the function is used by `type_getsets`. Please don't add `inline` in such refactoring change.

Same remark for `type_qualname()`.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -1492,28 +1498,29 @@ PyType_GetFullyQualifiedName(PyTypeObject *type)
     return _PyType_GetFullyQualifiedName(type, '.');
 }
 
-
-static PyObject *
-type_abstractmethods(PyTypeObject *type, void *context)
+static inline PyObject *
review_comments.body: Please don't add inline in such refactoring PR.
Ah right. I'm not even sure why I actually inlined the function. It doesn't even need to be inlined at first glance. I'll do it tomorrow.

Do you mean something like:

```c
PyObject *qualname = Py_NewRef(((PyHeapTypeObject *)type)->ht_qualname);
```

so that I don't double check `tp_flags`?
I would prefer to keep `PyObject *qualname = type_qualname((PyObject *)type, NULL);`.
